title: Evaluating TEM Sample Thickness for Enhanced Temperature Precision in Plasmon Energy Expansion Thermometry (PEET)
content: In-situ scanning/transmission electron microscopy (S/TEM) has become increasingly important for real-time characterization of microstructures in functional and structural materials under working and application conditions, as it reveals underlying structure-property relationships [1]. Recent advances in microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technology enable a very precise control of the in-situ stimuli [2], e.g. with a local temperature accuracy of 4% in in-situ TEM heating experiments [3]. Consequently, such MEMS heaters have been applied in studies of thermally-induce phase transformations in various material studies, such as in metal alloys [4, 5]. However, to achieve an accurate interpretation of temperature-correlated microstructure phenomena at the nanometer scale in such studies, the development of real-time and precise temperature measurement across the sample is very important.
